scope: These scenarios model conditional feasibility only; they are not a determination that any event occurred.

alternative_model.statement: One of the accession numbers is a later transcription error; 22 is compatible with the father dying at about forty.

cases.limits: The incompatibility is in current wording, not necessarily the reconstructed original Hebrew text.

research.claim: Conservative commentary attributes the 42 vs 22 disagreement to scribal transmission.
Parallel verses and Jehoram chronology are compared, with ancient versions discussed.

cases.focus: Whether both death narratives can describe one occurrence

assumptions: Hanging precedes a later fall; the latter report can describe consequences of death.

alternative_model.statement: The writers may preserve independent incompatible descriptions; the surviving passages alone cannot select.

cases.limits: An internally possible sequence is not evidence that the event happened.

research.claim: One tradition reconciles hanging followed by a fall.

cases.focus: Order in the Genesis 1 and 2 accounts

alternative_model.statement: Genesis 2 may narrow and retell Genesis 1, while historical-critical readings posit independent source traditions.

cases.limits: No historically testable observational timestamp for creation events; scientific claims require separately defined hypotheses.

research.claim: Literary and source-critical arguments for multiple creation accounts.

cases.focus: Whether Mark 16:9–20 belonged to earliest recoverable Gospel

alternative_model.statement: An early gospel text may have ended at 16:8 while other manuscript traditions preserved a longer ending.

cases.limits: Textual originality and factual historicity of narrated events must not be conflated.

research.claim: A peer-reviewed analysis cautions against misclassifying two Greek catena witnesses.
A scholar advocates the longer ending and discusses codex layout.
Sinaiticus and Vaticanus lack the longer ending in continuous text.

cases.focus: Whether Herod's lifetime and Quirinius's AD 6 census refer to the same birth

literal_model.note: BCE/CE years use signed integers only as a modeling shorthand; this case tests event ordering, not absolute year arithmetic.

alternative_model.statement: An otherwise undocumented census or alternate translation could change the assumptions; those claims require external evidence.

cases.limits: Disjoint source dates make that specific single-event reading impossible conditional on mainstream dates; not a verdict on all conceivable readings.

research.claim: Lexham summarizes the dated census and birth-narrative chronological tension.
A conservative historical analysis presents alternative earlier-governorship hypotheses with evidentiary limits.

cases.focus: Whether a young-Earth date is directly asserted in Genesis and independently supported

literal_model.premise_origin: later chronological inference, not these two verses

alternative_model.statement: Physical dating evidence overwhelmingly indicates Earth is billions of years old; the literal age inference is incompatible with that evidence.

cases.limits: Conflating one later interpretation with what a text expressly says is an invalid test.

research.claim: USGS discusses radiometric methods and geological age estimates.
Smithsonian describes fossil evidence for humans far older than a six-thousand-year timeline.
